issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies a Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(). However, the solution implementation of Pneumatic declares raisePressure(int) and releaseValve() (method name 'releaseValve' instead of 'openValve'), while the solution classes LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster implement a method named openValve(). This creates a signature/name mismatch between the interface and its implementing classes and contradicts the problem statement. As a result the provided solution is internally inconsistent and would not compile, and students would be confused about which method name to implement (openValve vs releaseValve).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface method names consistent with the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes. Preferably rename the method releaseValve() in solution/template to openValve() (void openValve()), and ensure all implementing classes override openValve(). Alternatively, if releaseValve() is intended, update the problem statement/UML and all implementing classes to use releaseValve() so the interface and implementations match.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Pneumatic interface method as openValve(), but the solution implementation declares releaseValve() in Pneumatic while the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) provide openValve(). This creates a direct naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation, causing confusion and a likely compile-time mismatch between the interface and its implementers.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the Pneumatic interface to openValve() to match the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes, or alternatively rename the implementing methods in LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster to releaseValve(). Prefer aligning the Pneumatic interface to openValve() so all artifacts (problem, template, solution) consistently use openValve().
